Subject: Re: Integration takeoff: NovusCare — Live-output & tool-calling cadence

Samir —

Appreciate the clear ask. I sketched a two-sprint takeoff (attached) focusing on:

1) Sprint 0 (3 days) — "air-bridge" validation: sample streaming session, prefix caching demo, and a small end-to-end: prompt -> function call -> structured JSON output.
2) Sprint 1 (2 weeks) — schema lock, event contract to your event bus (Kafka topic name + retention), tool call wiring (auth + rate limits), and a dry run with synthetic traffic.

Owners:
- Redwood infra & runtime: Ben Carter (will own the runtime knobs, batching profile, and fallback policy).
- CS/Implementation PM: Camila (me) — onboarding cadence, meetings, checklist.
- NovusCare engineering: Samir & Laura — event bus access, test accounts, and acceptance tests.

I've attached streaming_schema_v1_examples.json. Key asks for NovusCare before Sprint 0:
- Provide a dev Kafka topic and service account by Dec 6
- Confirm which functions you want Redwood to call (payment_check, claim_fetch) and any API keys
- Share 5 sample payloads for schema validation

Proposed check-in: daily 30m standups during Sprint 0, then M/W runbook reviews during Sprint 1. I'll send calendar invites once we confirm times.

Thanks —
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Camila@redwood.ai

Camila / team —

This looks sensible. A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- For structured outputs we prefer top-level fields (status, claim_id, risk_score) and a deterministic schema for downstream processors. Can you confirm Redwood will validate and reject malformed outputs during the dry run?
- For tool calling auth: we can issue short-lived API keys scoped to payment_check and claim_fetch; do you have a recommended rotation window?

Also, quick ask — can Ben share the initial batching profile he recommends for < 200 concurrent streams? That will help size our test harness.

Laura Chen
Senior Platform Engineer | NovusCare

Laura / Samir / Camila —

Quick answers:
- Runtime validation: yes — during the dry run we will run outputs through Redwood's schema gate. Malformed outputs will be tagged and sent to a dead-letter topic; we'll provide a validation report after each run.
- Batching profile (starter): target 64-token average response, max batch latency 75ms, dynamic splitting for function call paths. This profile scales well up to ~250 concurrent short sessions; we can tighten or loosen based on your latency SLOs.
- API key rotation: recommend 12-hour short-lived keys for function calls in the test window; for production we can move to scoped service accounts with KMS-backed secrets.

I'll attach a short config snippet in the shared Drive. Camila — please propose standup times; I can block mornings PT.

Ben Carter
Head of Runtime Integrations | Redwood Inference
